lens: final: the craft lens's 'Up Close' idea and product-truth discipline, run on the performance lens's chassis, with the festive lens's dated chapter grafted in
campaign_name: NAIRA Petite · Up Close · 2 Oct–11 Nov 2026 (slug upclose-oct26)
big_idea: Up close. This October the Indian jewellery feed is built to be read from across the room: 40–80% off, codes, sparkle, emoji. NAIRA builds for the opposite distance. Every ad is one in-stock piece (or one declared pair) and one true thing you only notice from a few inches away: the king fell and the hoops stayed, the rail left plain on purpose, a dome you can see light through, three colours instead of seven, a name that rearranges into A RAIN, nine hearts for nine nights. It is said in one Velista line and/or one lowercase Cormorant turn, with the piece named at its live price and exact material line in a quiet Jost caption, and the piece's own story told in the primary text. Three chapters share that grammar. The finish, seen up close: the account's one clear win. The house that sews: spool, swatch, care label, pattern key, because NAIRA is a couture house first. And a dated festive chapter where the true detail meets the date: nine hearts for Navratri, two stones that don't match for Karwa Chauth, a prism that brings its own light for Diwali, two hearts that make a bow for Bhai Dooj. Permanence is never shouted on the image. It is proved as finish that survives a close look, and the founder's 'made to stay gold.' closes the primary text of every gold-coated or two-tone piece. Prism Rivière, the only rhodium-only hero, closes on 'NAIRA Petite.' until the founder approves a rhodium variant.
why_it_wins: 1. It is the judges' consensus, built the way they asked. Two of the three judges scored the craft lens's 'Up Close' first (47.7 vs 46.4 and 46.2; 46 vs 45.5 and 41), and the third scored it a close second (7.9 vs 8.0) while asking for its best briefs and its stock guard. All three asked for the performance lens's media chassis, and two asked for the festive lens's dated frames. This plan is that combination: the craft idea and its product-truth discipline, the performance structure, and the festive frames that survive the never-list. 2. It rests on the account's clearest result, not on taste. In the same ad set 'finished to be seen up close' beat 'daily wear' 3.8 to 2.2 add-to-carts per ₹1,000 (p≈0.002) and 10 orders to 2. The only static with repeat orders was one piece, one tactile metaphor and a paradox line, with the piece's own story in the copy (49 add-to-carts at ₹115, ROAS 1.62); the same image with edit-and-price copy got 3. All 7 orders won by single-product statics bought the pictured piece, and 6 of them were prepaid. So every brief is one piece or a declared pair, one up-close truth and that piece's story, and no image carries an offer, a code or a percentage. 3. It takes the one position the season leaves open. Offer tiles are 22% of category ads, discounts run 40–80%, 'artisan' appears in 0 live Indian ads, nobody runs macro, and 1 of 24 tracked brands mentions Karwa Chauth. Quiet, detailed and owned is the loudest position available, and BUY2's 10% could never win the discount race anyway. 4. It puts the money where the stock and the proof are. 15 of the 26 briefs feature one of the six deep-stock pieces (Toggle Link Chain 80 units, Woven Gold Hoops 77, Prism Rivière 76, Heartbead 29, Brushed Gold Huggies 16, Baroque Shell 13; Shopify, 1 Oct), and 13 feature the five pieces that have already sold through ads. Every other piece has at least 3 units, the 1–2-unit SKUs are out, and a stock guard pauses any ad when its piece reaches 1. 5. It builds the basket without discounting the picture: three declared pairs (₹2,598, ₹3,598 and ₹3,698; the two larger ones clear the ₹3,000 free-shipping line even after BUY2) and BUY2 in every primary text, against 1.33 items per order and only 6 of 43 orders over ₹3,000. 6. It gives Meta's Andromeda 26 genuinely different candidates: 26 layout architectures across about a dozen visual worlds (plaster, chess, spool, cardamom, folded paper, prism light, silk and linen on model, packshots in drawn frames), each with a separately composed 9:16 for Stories, the cheapest add-to-cart placement and the source of all three Woven orders. 7. It fixes the money leaks the data shows: one campaign instead of two overlapping ones, Feed, Stories and FB Feed only, no cost cap, verdicts on Shopify-verified orders and add-to-carts per ₹1,000 (never CTR), a stop-loss, and the funnel fixes that cap any creative. Honest limit: creative alone will not close a 3.2x gap (₹3,320 per order now against ₹1,047 break-even). The realistic target is a blended ₹1,600 per order by 27 Oct, and break-even on the concepts that clearly win.
festive_timing: Dates come from the festive calendar in the competitor research (checked 1 Oct); none is a shipping cut-off. 2–10 Oct, Pitru Paksha (to Sarva Pitru Amavasya, 10 Oct), when many families avoid new jewellery and tracked brands hold festival naming: Wave 1 only (C01–C12), with no festival named and no gifting frame anywhere; read add-to-carts cheaply before metro CPMs rise. 11 Oct (Ghatasthapana): Wave 2 opens. C14 'NINE NIGHTS.' runs 11–19 Oct only and is off at 00:00 on 20 Oct (Dussehra). Gifting and festive colour start (C13 pair, C15 deep green on cream, C16 pearl pair, C17 season line, C18 sizer rings), with no festival named except in C17's copy. 18–28 Oct: C19 'YOU AND ME.' for Karwa Chauth, off at 23:59 on 28 Oct. The image names the festival but carries no date, and the copy states none, because sources split between 28 and 29 October. 25 Oct–8 Nov: C20 'FESTIVAL OF LIGHTS.' and C21 'DIWALI LIST / 1. me.' run through Dhanteras (6 Nov) and Diwali (Sunday 8 Nov) and are off at 23:59 on 8 Nov. No Dhanteras frame and no 'buy gold' framing anywhere, because the pieces are coated. From 25 Oct the break-even cost per order tightens to about ₹830 as festive COD returns rise. 1–11 Nov: C22 'NOT AN ENVELOPE THIS YEAR.' for Bhai Dooj (Wednesday 11 Nov; brothers shop ahead), off at 23:59 on 11 Nov. 12 Nov: every festive frame is off; the evergreen winners and their weekly re-cuts continue. Total budget does not rise with festive CPMs; dated ads take share inside AS1. Durga Pujo (Bengal) and Dasara (Maharashtra) frames are left out: at this budget a single-geo ad set cannot reach a verdict, and the Dasara 'gold' custom sits too close to gold claims. No ad states a delivery date or an order-by line, because no courier cut-off is confirmed. If the founder confirms real cut-offs, they go into the primary text only.
structure: OBJECTIVE: one Sales campaign, 'NAIRA Petite · Up Close · Oct26', conversion event Purchase (pixel and CAPI), Highest Volume, no cost or bid cap (the ₹213 and ₹450–750 caps starved delivery), attribution 7-day click and 1-day view, with every verdict made on Shopify-verified orders. It replaces both live campaigns: pause 'one winner – Copy' and 'Naira · IG Top 20' (no delivery yet) at launch, so about ₹2,200 a day stops splitting across overlapping auctions. Ad 104 is paused too, not kept as a benchmark, because its image prints 'SURGICAL STEEL', 'SHOP THE EDIT' and 'FROM ₹899'; its story copy lives on in C01. The creator reels stop with that campaign. Advantage+ creative enhancements are off (no auto-animation, brightness changes or added text), so what ships is what was checked. AD SETS (ad-set budgets): AS1 Prospecting · Broad: the seven metros of the old 'Metro A' set (broad, no interests; the account's best set, 12 orders on ₹38,972) with Advantage+ audience on and women 30–50 as the suggestion. Women 35–44 placed 42% of orders on 32% of spend; men convert at the same rate per rupee and often buy two pieces, so they are not excluded. Purchasers of the last 14 days are excluded. AS1 holds 22 briefs in three waves, at most 10 live at once. AS2 Warm · Second look (Stories-first): website visitors 30 days (PageView), Instagram and Facebook engagers 60 days and 25% viewers of the two collab reels, purchasers of the last 14 days excluded, Advantage+ audience off. It holds 4 briefs (the pair upsell and three slow reads), all live at once. AS2 launches only when Meta estimates at least 10,000 people; the old VC30 + cart14 pools were about 20 people at ₹1,067–1,587 CPM. Until then its slow-read ads wait (they never run in prospecting) and its ₹300 stays in AS1. If AS2 is not live by 11 Oct, only C23, an instant-read pair, moves into AS1 Wave 2. Pause AS2 if its CPM is above ₹600 after ₹1,500. PLACEMENTS: Instagram Feed, Instagram Stories and Facebook Feed only, with placement asset customisation: the 4:5 master in feeds and its separately composed 9:16 in Stories. Exclude Instagram Reels: ₹21,368 there bought 7 orders at ROAS 0.55, below Feed's 0.76 and Stories' 0.84, with only 36% of its landing views firing ViewContent, and these ads are statics. Also exclude Facebook Reels, Facebook Stories, Audience Network, WhatsApp Status, Threads, Explore and Messenger (about ₹6,700 there bought no order). BUDGET: a base of ₹2,000 a day (AS1 ₹1,700, AS2 ₹300), or ₹82,000 over 41 days, below today's run-rate of about ₹2,200 a day. From 11 Oct, raise AS1 by 20% every 72 hours, up to ₹2,800 a day, but only while the trailing-7-day blended Shopify-verified cost per order is at or under ₹1,600 and at least one ad has passed. From 28 Oct, keep the highest daily budget that held it at or under ₹1,300. Hard cap ₹1,05,000 including all scaling. ROTATION: Wave 1 (2 Oct): C01–C10 live, except that C10 gets no budget until the Chevron Whisper Ring page is corrected; C11 (once its product page is fixed) and C12 enter as the first slots free. Wave 2 (11 Oct): C14 goes live on 11 Oct because it is dated; C13, C15, C16, C17 and C18 follow as Wave 1 ads are cut or starved. Wave 3 (dated): C19 on 18 Oct, C20 and C21 on 25 Oct, C22 on 1 Nov. On each start date, pause the live AS1 ad with the weakest add-to-carts per ₹1,000 among those that have had their verdict, so AS1 stays at 10. AS2, once live: C23–C26. Each ad is one ad carrying both placements' assets. NAMING: campaign 'NAIRA Petite · Up Close · Oct26'; ad sets 'AS1 · Prospecting · 7 metros · Broad' and 'AS2 · Warm · Second look'; ads '<id> · <ad set> · <wave> · <role> · <product> · <short idea>', for example 'C03 · AS1 · W1 · hook · Woven Gold Hoops · king fell'. Files are C03_woven-gold-hoops_4x5.jpg and C03_woven-gold-hoops_9x16.jpg. Every URL carries utm_source=meta, utm_medium=paid_social, utm_campaign=upclose-oct26 and utm_content=<id>, so Shopify orders match by utm_content. Until UTMs are captured, orders are matched by order time and value, as the research did. KPIs: (1) Shopify-verified cost per ad-won order: break-even ₹1,047 at today's ₹2,198 AOV, and about ₹830 from 25 Oct as festive COD returns rise; interim goal a blended ₹1,600 by 27 Oct (₹3,320 now). (2) Add-to-carts per ₹1,000 at 3 or more (account 3.3, the Prism winner 8.7), read only once the duplicate AddToCart sender is gone. (3) Basket: AOV at least ₹2,600, at least 1.5 items per order, at least 25% of orders over ₹3,000, and BUY2 on at least 20% of orders. (4) Prepaid share at least 60% (42% of orders are COD now). (5) Diagnostics: the share of orders containing the pictured piece, saves and shares per 1,000 impressions by concept (the memory test), CTR and CPM. CTR is never a verdict: the higher-CTR variants lost on carts and orders. KILL / HOLD / SCALE: an ad is judged at about ₹3,500 spent, or at day 7 if it has spent at least ₹1,500 by then. Under ₹700 by day 7 means Meta starved it, so it is rotated out without a verdict. Pass: at least 3 add-to-carts per ₹1,000 and at least 1 verified order. Kill: under 3 per ₹1,000 and no order at ₹3,500, or no add-to-cart at ₹2,000. In between, hold for one more week. Dated ads cannot wait that long: an early read at ₹1,500 or day 4 pauses any with zero add-to-carts, and the rest run to the end of their window and are judged on it. Scale a concept, not an ad: at 3 or more verified orders at ₹1,300 or less each, re-cut it weekly (a new crop, or the same line on another deep-stock piece, the Missoma and Monica Vinader model), keep the original running, and raise AS1 by 20% every 72 hours while blended cost per order stays at or under ₹1,300. Refresh creative when 7-day frequency passes 2.5 in AS1 or 4 in AS2. Stock guard (Shopify, checked every Monday): pause a single-piece ad when its piece reaches 1 unit, and a pair ad when either piece does; never write scarcity. Stop-loss: if ₹40,000 is spent and blended verified cost per order is above ₹2,500, cut AS1 to ₹1,000 a day, switch AS2 off, keep only passing ads and fix the funnel before spending more. Every verdict states its Poisson interval: nothing on fewer than about 20 orders is established. PRE-LAUNCH (these cap any creative): charge 3% GST for HSN 7117 instead of 18%; remove the duplicate server AddToCart sender; capture UTMs on the headless storefront; check fastrr checkout completion (add-to-cart to checkout fell to about 25–30%); confirm in Shopify that BUY2 gives 10% on two or more pieces, including two of the same piece, and how the ₹3,000 free-shipping bar treats the discount (both pairs that mention it clear it either way). Correct five product pages that the ads must never echo before their ads send traffic: the Toggle Link Chain page says 'closes with a turn rather than a catch' and 'toggle bar and ring clasp', but the piece ships with a spring-ring clasp and a pavé-set gate (C05, C13, C21); the Granule Dome Ring page says 'solid gold granulation', but the dome is an openwork lattice (C11); the Halo Curve Ring page says 'solid gold band' (C19); and the Chevron Whisper Ring page still says 'A band that comes to a soft point. This ring is shaped as a double V, with two fine pave lines...' and 'Profile: Double V chevron band' (products_1.json, updated 30 Sep; the live storefront returned 404 and could not be checked), so a click on ONE LEFT PLAIN. lands on copy that never mentions the plain rail and calls the sharp point soft. Rewrite it as three fine rails, a sharp-pointed stone-set V, a plain polished softer V and a gently curved stone-set rail, meeting in one plain band (profile: 'Three rails meeting in one plain band'), and give C10 no budget until the page reads that way. The Verdant Circlet Studs page says 'a white shell pearl of about 6mm resting inside the circle' and 'Pearl: White shell pearl, approximately 6mm, inside the circlet', but each stud carries two white shell pearls of about 6 mm and 4 mm, as C15's primary text says; C15 gets no spend until the page names both. Confirm the Heartbead bead finish (the tags say Rhodium Plated, the page says silver-tone steel) behind the '[ 18k gold coated · rhodium coated ]' line (C07, C23). Count the hearts on a physical Heartline Paperclip Necklace (the audit counts nine) before C14. Ask the founder whether rhodium-only pieces get a sign-off variant; until then, Prism-only ads close on 'NAIRA Petite.'. Decide on a prepaid incentive or a three-piece BUY rung; no ad mentions either until it exists.

A prism takes one beam of light and lets it come apart, and this bracelet does the same along one line of cushion-cut stones, aqua blue, soft pink and pale yellow in turn, each framed in a fine halo of tiny clear stones. A fold-over clasp keeps the line flat on the wrist, and the links adjust from 15 to 19 cm. Worn alone, it is enough.
